rules.statement: Return plaintext secret material only in the response of the operation that creates (or rotates) the secret; no read path (GET by id, list, preview, update/PUT) may ever return it.
rules.why: Any path that returns material on read is a standing liability: every later read, cache, log and audit record becomes a place the secret can leak from, and it breaks the metadata-only retrieval rule.
rules.check: Look for GET/list/preview/PUT handlers or response models that include secret values, key bytes or an encoded secret field. Only create/rotate responses may carry material.

rules.statement: Model a one-time secret reveal as a separate create-only response type that extends the metadata resource, not as an optional or nullable material property on the shared resource type that read paths return.
rules.why: An optional, usually-null field on the type every read path returns makes leakage a question of review discipline. A separate create-only type makes the guarantee hold by construction.
rules.check: Flag a secret/value/material property added to a resource DTO that GET/list endpoints also return, and flag read endpoints declared to return the create-only reveal type.

rules.statement: Endpoints that create secrets the server holds for itself (its own signing or encryption keys) must return a type with no material field, and must not share a create handler or response type with endpoints that do reveal material.
rules.why: Scoping the reveal by owner makes those endpoints structurally unable to return private material, whatever secret type is generated. A runtime type check would wrongly reveal a symmetric server key.
rules.check: Look for server- or tenant-owned secret create endpoints that return a reveal-capable type, or a single shared create handler or response type used for every owner kind.

rules.statement: Never return asymmetric private key material from an API, and never have the server generate a keypair for an external party and hand back the private key. Reveal only symmetric shared secrets, and set the material to null for RSA and EC keys.
rules.why: A server-minted private key sent over the wire is exactly the exposure that server-side generation exists to prevent. Asymmetric client authentication (private_key_jwt) uses keypairs that the client generates itself.
rules.check: Check reveal code paths for a guard that fills the material only when the secret type is symmetric. Flag any code that generates RSA/EC keys for a client and serializes the private key into a response.

rules.statement: Keep unprotected secret material out of every durable or diagnostic sink: audit events, logs, traces and persisted records may hold only metadata and the data-protected encoded value.
rules.why: The one-time plaintext must exist only in the single authorized HTTP response. Any copy in a sink becomes a permanent leak surface.
rules.check: Look for the plaintext/unprotected secret or the reveal response object being passed to loggers, audit events, activity tags or exception messages, or being persisted without data protection.
